title: Electric and Magnetic Fields
seo_title: Electric Field Worksheets: Field Lines, E = F/q and Energy in Fields (High School Physics)
standard_text: Develop and use a model of two objects interacting through electric or magnetic fields to illustrate the forces between objects and the changes in energy of the objects due to the interaction.
meta_desc: Free high school physics worksheets on electric and magnetic fields (NGSS HS-PS3-5): field lines, field strength E = F/q, forces on charges and energy stored in fields. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Fields carry forces and store energy.
key_sub: Moving objects against a field force stores energy; moving with it releases energy.
body_html:
How to think about it

Objects interact through fields, and fields store energy.

  • Electric field lines go from + to −; magnetic field lines go from N to S outside a magnet. Closer lines = stronger field.
  • E = F ÷ q. A positive charge is pushed along the field; a negative charge the opposite way.
  • Moving objects against the field force stores energy (like lifting a mass); moving with it releases energy as motion.
Example

2 μC feels 0.004 N. E?

0.004 ÷ 0.000002

Answer: 2,000 N/C

Example

Pull apart two attracting magnets?

Work against the force

Answer: stored energy increases

Common mistakes

  • Thinking field lines point toward positive charges.
  • Thinking stored energy always drops when objects move apart.
  • Thinking a negative charge moves along the field lines.

faq.a: A region around a charge where other charges feel a force. Its strength is E = F ÷ q.

faq.q: How do field lines show direction and strength?
faq.a: Arrows show the direction of the force on a positive test charge (or a north pole), and closer lines mean a stronger field.
Pulling attracting objects apart or pushing repelling objects together takes work, which is stored in the field, just like lifting a mass in Earth's gravitational field.
